la:adj:lividus.html:
līvĭdus, a, um, adj.
liveo
,
of a blue or leaden color, bluish, blue.
Lit.: vada,: lividissima vorago,: racemi,.—
Esp., produced by beating, bruising, etc., black and blue, livid: livida armis Bracchia,: ora livida facta,; .—
Transf., making livid, i. e. deadly: livida materno fervent adipata veneno,.—
Trop., envious, invidious, spiteful, malicious.
Of persons: invidi et malevoli et lividi, (dub.): nos nostraque lividus odit,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: lingua,: obliviones (because forgetfulness robs the deserving of the praise which is his due),: sententia,spiteful, malicious,.—Hence, līvĭdē, adv., of a leaden color, lividly.—Comp., dub.

la:verb:livido.html:
līvĭdo, āre, v. a.
id.
,

la:noun:livor.html:
līvor, ōris, m.
liveo
,
bluish color, leaden color, a black and blue spot.
Lit.: jam livorem tute scapulis istoc concinnas tuis,: livore decoloratum corpus mortui,: ostendere nigram in facie tumidis livoribus offam,; ; cf. ; ; : illinitur livoribus,.—Of a speck or taint in fruit: uva conspectā livorem ducit ab uva,: tum sucos herbasque dedi queis livor abiret,.—
Trop., envy, spite, malice, ill-will (mostly poet. and post-Aug. for invidia): summā malevolentiā et livore impediuntur, Brut. ap. : obtrectatio et livor,: pascitur in vivis livor; post fata quiescit,: ergo submotum patriā proscindere, livor, Desine,: rumpere, livor edax,: cupidus,: livor ac malignitas,; ; .

senses: Livius Andronicus a Roman dramatist and poet
la:other:Livius.html:
Līvĭus, i, m. (-a, ae, f.),
name of a Roman gens.—So, M. Livius Andronicus, the first Roman tragic poet, ; : T. Livius,the celebrated historian,: C. Livius Salinator, consul with L. Valerius Messala, A. U. C. 584; ; ; and many others.—In fem.: Līvĭa, ae, Drusilla, the second wife of Augustus, ; ; ; ; : Livia Orestilla,wife of Caligula,.—Hence,
Līvĭus, a, um, adj., Livian: Liviae leges,: familia,: arbos,.—
Līvĭānus, a, um, adj., Livian: modi, i. e. of Livius Andronicus, : exercitus, the army of the consul M. Livius, : aes,from mines belonging to Livia,: charta,named after Livia,; cf. § 74.
